sector_model: nonfinancial consumer subscription software; GAAP earnings with tax normalization, FCF after capex and capitalized software, SBC deducted, net cash from cash and investments
thesis: Duolingo (language-learning app, 64.9M DAUs, 13.1M paid subscribers) rallied 25% on 2026-11-04 after Q3 results to 160.42 (close 2026-11-06). Market cap about 7.57B and EV about 6.08B after 1.48B cash and investments with no borrowings. DAU growth reaccelerated to +29% (from +23%), 9M26 revenue +19%, TTM FCF about 396M (5.2% yield, 6.5% on EV). Guidance FY26 revenue 1,221M (+18%), adjusted EBITDA 323M (26.5%).
counterthesis: GAAP earnings are thin: TTM net income 145.7M gives about 52x P/E; Q3 operating income fell to 24.2M from 35.2M and Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 25.5% from 29.5%. Bookings growth (+12% Q3, 11% 9M) trails DAU growth (+29%), so monetization per user is lagging and management says it is leaning into monetization and sunsetting the Max tier. SBC of about 157M TTM is 40% of FCF (FCF after SBC about 239M, 3.2% yield). A securities class action was filed 2026-10-07 (no accrual). Q3 gross margin 72.9% is guided to 72.0% in Q4 as AI features roll out; AI assistants can substitute for the product. A stock that moved from 128 to 161 in two sessions has re-rated sharply, so the price no longer reflects the pre-earnings pessimism. Q3 includes an 11.4M accrual tied to Q4 DAU growth target. Peer and history multiples not gathered.
invalidation: DAU growth falling below 20% with bookings growth under 10%; gross margin falling below 70%; FCF after SBC declining year on year; operating margin below 8% on a TTM basis; adverse class action outcome or evidence of material user migration to general AI assistants.
